name: density-behavior
title: Density behavior
summary: A 200×200 card with a 1 dp border, 16 dp padding and 14 sp text, declared in dp so the player scales it to any screen density.
prompt: A 200×200 card with a 1 dp hairline border, 16 dp padding and 14 sp text that looks identical on 1x, 2x and 3x screens.
teaches: Declare that sizes are in dp with header.densityBehavior 2 (0 legacy, 1 pixels, 2 dp)
Let the player scale the document size, padding, spacedBy gaps, borders and fixed sizes by the display density
Draw a 1 dp rounded hairline as a clipped accent box with 1 dp padding around a clipped dark box

snippets.note: 2 = DENSITY_BEHAVIOR_DP: the header size and the layout values are dp
a 1 dp hairline: clip 12 + accent background + padding 1, around a clip 11 dark card with 16 dp padding

check.describe: At density 1 the card fills 200×200 with a thin blue frame. In the Java reference at 400×400 and density 2 the outer padding becomes 32 px and the 8 dp spacedBy gap 16 px. Resized (140×200, 300×160) the card keeps 16 dp padding and 1 dp hairline; the body text rewraps to the width.

pitfalls: Without densityBehavior (legacy, 0) the Java reference does not scale padding or fixed width/height by density: at density 2 a 16 padding stays 16 px. Only densityBehavior 2 makes them dp

densityBehavior needs apiLevel 8: the Java parser refuses it at 7. At apiLevel 8 the border modifier is written in its non-legacy form (json2rc matches Java); its width is dp and scales too. The border is drawn inside the bounds, so pad by width + spacing (17 here) to keep the content clear of it
Compare layouts at density 2 with players/conformance/java-layout.sh doc.rc 400 400 --density 2; the C++ player matches, the TypeScript player is being fixed (EXAMPLES_FINDINGS T7)
border's cornerRadius only rounds with "shape": 2 (ROUNDED_RECTANGLE); the default shape 0 is a plain rectangle in Java, whatever the radius
